$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for app/service identity and wiring.
Adding an app to this monorepo used to mean touching eight unrelated files, with
nothing cross-validating them; five of them had quietly drifted apart by
2026-08-17 (see docs/todo/erp2-program/01-registry-drift-report.md). Every one of
those surfaces is now checked against this file by scripts/js/verify-app-wiring.js,
which fails the build on any disagreement.
WHAT LIVES HERE: identity and wiring — key, systemd unit, workspace directory,
port, api-pro domains, launcher category, and the flags that record a DELIBERATE
divergence so it can never be mistaken for drift again.
WHAT DOES NOT: presentation (label, icon, description). Those stay in
packages/pos-shared/lib/roles.js APP_META until the admin console's app-catalogue
work (docs/todo/admin-console-program/01-app-catalogue-entitlements.md) moves the
catalogue server-side per tenant. Baking titles in here now would be work undone
the moment a tenant can enable its own app set.
DERIVED, NOT STORED (the validator computes and checks these):
envPrefix  workspace uppercased, '-' -> '_'   pos-auth      -> POS_AUTH__PORT
urlVar     workspace minus pos-/rutba- prefix rutba-web-user -> NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_USER_URL
An entry only carries `urlVar` when it deliberately breaks that rule.
FLAGS (absent = the common case):
public        no access grant needed; always in the catalogue, never in VALID_APP_KEYS
npmWorkspace  false = installs standalone via `npm --prefix` (the two backends)
build         false = has no build step, so no root build:* script is expected
launcher      false = not a launchable app, so no roles.js APP_URLS entry
descriptorScan false = excluded from APP_FOLDERS in discover-descriptor-meta.mjs
`rename` — THE ERP 2.0 P3 TARGET, NOT THE CURRENT STATE.
Declared here ahead of the move so the target is reviewable and machine-readable
before a single directory shifts; scripts/js/restructure.js is the only thing that
reads it, and verify-app-wiring.js ignores it entirely until the sweep lands and
the fields above are overwritten with these values. Plan and rationale:
docs/todo/erp2-program/03-repo-restructure.md.
path       new directory, relative to the repo root
key        new app key — the X-Rutba-App value and the api-pro domain
unit       new systemd unit name
envPrefix  new PREFIX__ for this app's env vars
urlVar     new NEXT_PUBLIC_*_URL
domains    new api-pro domain keys (absent = unchanged)
roles      old role key -> new role key (absent = unchanged). EXPLICIT, never
derived: today's prefixes do not follow the domain (order-management
-> order_*, web-user -> webuser_*, web -> web_public/web_user), so a
derivation rule would silently mint the wrong key for four domains.
Grants survive a key change on their own — up_users_app_roles_lnk
references app_role_id, not the key — so this is an UPDATE of
api_pro_app_roles.key, not a re-grant. Measured 2026-08-18: 69 of the
79 roles are held by at least one user.

services.note: Legacy Strapi backend. Retires in ERP 2.0 phase P2; every frontend reaches it via NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, not a per-app URL var.

rename.why: envPrefix deliberately NOT renamed. POS_STRAPI__ carries the DATABASE_* values rutba-core falls back to, and ~20 keys of it live in every deploy env including the LAN box's off-git master file. The whole block dies with pos-strapi in P2, so renaming it now buys two coordinated live-env edits and nothing that outlives them.

services.note: Koa/Knex backend serving the same descriptor contract. Plain Node — no bundling step, hence build:false. Shares NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL with strapi because RUTBA_BACKEND picks which one listens.

rename.why: RUTBA_CORE__ -> CORE__. Needs the precedence chain in src/config/env.js updated in the same commit (CORE__NAME > POS_STRAPI__NAME > NAME).
'web' names the technology, not the thing. This is the public shop.
apps/sales/sale is the repetition this sweep exists to kill, and the app IS the point-of-sale terminal.
'web-user' reads as a user type, not an app. It is the customer self-service portal.
The three accounts-* sub-domains are authorization-only and keep their keys — they name permission scopes, not apps.
Also drops the hardcoded `-p 4012` in its package.json scripts (drift report A6) — the only app not taking PORT from load-env.js.
Longest name in the estate, and its roles already disagreed with it (order_* under domain order-management).
Long, but kept in full: 'mfg' is the core module's internal name and would be cryptic on a user-facing app.
Roles stay ess_employee/ess_manager — this domain has never had the admin/manager/staff triple.

apps/inventory/inventory is absurd, and 'stock' vs 'inventory' has never been separable by name. Its pages are levels, transfers, counts, adjustments, valuation, expiry and reorder — inventory control. 'stock' keeps products and purchasing.

apps/admin/admin, and admin_admin, are both self-parody. Drops the deprecated `users` alias in the same move: users_admin/manager/staff are held by zero users (measured 2026-08-18), so the alias can go rather than be carried into the new tree. NOTE: this claims the name `console`, so P5's control plane becomes services/control-plane rather than rutba-console.

services.note: Background sync worker sharing the rutba-marketplace workspace. No HTTP surface, so no port and no URL var; the registry records its port as '-'.

rename.why: Still shares the app's workspace and env block. Extracting it to services/marketplace-worker is P3 follow-up work, not part of the move — it needs its own package.json and dependency set first.
Already correct. The descriptor contract is the API; renaming it would churn 390 files for nothing.
Nothing about it is point-of-sale — it holds roles.js, the app catalogue and shared UI for all 22 apps. The single largest rewrite in the sweep: 405 files import it.
'-core' meant 'the core of sync', but rutba-core is a different thing entirely and the collision misleads.
Left alone deliberately: the plugin wrapper retires in P2 once enforcement moves into rutba-core/src/policy/. Renaming a component with a scheduled death date is churn.
Same: its Strapi peer dependency retires in P2 and the provider logic lives on inside core's upload platform.

domainsWithoutApps.why: rutba-users was replaced by rutba-admin, which inherited port 4022. The domain stays alive as an alias so existing users_* grants keep resolving. Retires in ERP 2.0 phase P3 with the alias sweep.

rename.why: Measured 2026-08-18: users_admin, users_manager and users_staff are held by ZERO users, so the alias protects nothing. Deleted by the restructure rather than carried into the new tree.

domainsWithoutApps.why: Present in domains.json with no app, no workspace and no catalogue entry. Either a planned domain or vestigial — flagged in the registry drift report (A3) as a decision that is still owed.

rename.why: Measured 2026-08-18: 15 users hold delivery_admin/manager/staff. Whatever its origin, it is live — so the restructure carries it unchanged and the decision stays owed. Deleting it would revoke access from 15 people.
